title: Why is the sky blue? (it's not the ocean)

analogy.limitation: Light is not really a ball; it is a wave, and blue waves are shorter.

claims.claim: Sunlight looks white but is made of all the colors of the rainbow
Blue light has shorter waves and is scattered more by the atmosphere than red
At sunset light passes through more air so more blue is scattered away, leaving reds and oranges
The ocean is blue mainly because water absorbs red light (not because it mirrors the sky)

sources.claim: NASA SpacePlace: Why is the sky blue?
NOAA: Why is the ocean blue?

style.illustration_style: children's picture book illustration, soft gouache and colored pencil texture, bright cheerful candy colors, thick friendly outlines, rounded cute shapes, simple uncluttered background, warm sunny light, vertical 9:16 composition, absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no words

cast.pip: Pip, a curious little owl with round glasses and a yellow scarf
cast.tia: Tia, a girl of about seven in a green hoodie with two black pigtails
cast.sunny: Sunny, a cheerful cartoon sun with a round smiling face

scenes.narration: Is the sky blue because it copies the ocean? Nope! The sky has its own trick.

visual.prompt: {tia} and {pip} stand on a grassy hill looking up at a bright blue sky, with a calm blue sea far behind them, wide shot, sunny day

scenes.narration: Sunlight looks white, but it is secretly a bag of rainbow colors.

visual.prompt: {sunny} happily tips open a big cloth bag and rainbow-colored bouncy balls (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, violet) tumble out, {pip} watches amazed, medium shot, simple sky background

scenes.narration: Imagine those colors are bouncy balls, rolling through a playground full of tiny bumpers.

visual.prompt: colorful bouncy balls rolling down a playground slope full of little round bumper pegs like a pinball board, bright cheerful, {tia} watches from the side, medium wide shot

scenes.narration: Little blue balls hit every bumper and bounce everywhere. Big red balls roll straight through.

visual.prompt: many small blue bouncy balls bouncing in all directions off round bumper pegs, while a few big red balls roll straight through the middle in a clean line, close shot, playful

scenes.narration: Grown-ups call that bouncing scattering. Blue scatters the most. So blue reaches your eyes from everywhere in the sky.

visual.prompt: {tia} looks up wide-eyed at a sky full of tiny sparkling blue dots drifting everywhere, {pip} points upward beside her, medium shot, big sky

scenes.narration: At sunset, light travels through more air. The blue bounces away, and the reds and oranges are left.

visual.prompt: a glowing orange and pink sunset over a calm hill, {tia} and {pip} sit together watching it, {sunny} sinking low on the horizon, wide shot, warm light

scenes.narration: Light is not really a ball, of course. It is a wave, and blue waves are just shorter.

visual.prompt: {pip} holds up two ribbons, a short wiggly blue ribbon and a long smooth red ribbon, side by side, {tia} nods, close shot, plain pastel background

scenes.narration: So the sky's trick is bouncing blue light. Send this to someone who looks up a lot!

visual.prompt: {tia} and {pip} wave happily toward the viewer under a bright blue sky, {sunny} smiling above them, sparkles, medium shot
